questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the simple past correctly with an irregular verb?

options.text: She goed to the market yesterday.
She went to the market yesterday.
She has went to the market yesterday.
She was go to the market yesterday.

questions.explanation: "yesterday" is an indicator of the past, so the verb takes the simple past, and "go" is irregular: its past form is "went". "goed" adds -ed to an irregular verb; "has went" puts the simple past after "has", where the past participle "gone" is needed; "was go" mixes "be" with a base verb.

questions.prompt: What is the correct form for a simple past question with a regular verb?
questions.explanation: A simple past question is Did + subject + base verb: "Did she walk to school?" The past is already carried by "did", so "walked" after it marks the past twice; "Was she walk" uses "be" instead of "did", and "Does" is present.

questions.prompt: Complete: "At nine o'clock last night, Amine ___ his lessons."
questions.explanation: The revision was in progress at nine o'clock last night, so we use the past progressive: was/were + verb + ing. "Amine" is one person (he), so the auxiliary is "was": Amine was revising. "were revising" is for you, we and they; "was revise" forgets the -ing; "is revising" is present.

questions.prompt: Which word is associated with the present perfect, NOT the simple past?
questions.explanation: "already" is one of the words that usually go with the present perfect (have/has + past participle), like just, recently and lately. "yesterday", "last year" and "in 2020" all give a finished time, so they go with the simple past.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the present perfect correctly?

options.text: She has visited Rome last summer.
She have visited Rome many times.

questions.explanation: "She has visited Rome twice" is an experience with no finished time: has + past participle. "last summer" is a finished time, which needs the simple past (She visited Rome last summer); "she have" breaks the agreement (she takes has); "has visit" forgets the past participle.
